div.div: Q. 1 فَرْشَحَ , inf. n. فَرْشَحَةٌ (S, K) and فَرْشَحَى, (K,) He (a man, S) parted his legs; (K:) or he parted his legs in sitting; and so فَرْشَطَ: (Lh, S:) or he spread his legs wide apart: (A 'Obeyd, TA:) and he stood with his legs wide apart in prayer; (Ks, S;) and so فرشح رِجْلَيْهِ: (S:) or he sat in a relaxed state, with his thighs cleaving to the ground; (K;) and so فَرْشَطَ: (TA:) or he leaped, or jumped; (K;) or made short leaps or jumps. (TA.) And فَرْشَحَتْ, (S, L, and so in some copies of the K,) or ↓ تَفَرْشَحَتْ , (thus in other copies of the K, and thus in the CK,) She (a camel) parted her kind legs to be milked (S, L, K) and to stale. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
